I think there's a bit of confusion here. The way the code currently works is once the discovery application starts, it begins waiting for BMC Ready, using the PowerRestoreDelay value for the maximum amount of time it will wait for BMC Ready. It checks every 1s, so as soon as BMC Ready is hit, the host boot will be started. Although the discover service actually doesn't run until BMC Ready so it all kind of just happens at the same time (BMC Ready hit, APR policy enforced).

My understanding is you wanted the boot to start even sooner then BMC Ready. i.e. start once the bare minimum of BMC services are running. In that case we need to go back to https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-state-manager/+/71085 where we changed the discover app to wait for BMC Ready (After=multi-user.target) and put that behind a meson feature (only-allow-boot-when-bmc-ready). So on your system, you set the PowerRestoreDelay to 0, and don't enable only-allow-boot-when-bmc-ready.

I found a bug while working on this feature. The bug:
1) User sets PowerRestorePolicy as AlwaysOn
2) User sets PowerRestoreDelay as 120 seconds
3) User performs GracefulShutdown
4) User does AC power cycle
Once, the BMC is up the expectation is to apply Power Policy that is AlwaysOn after 120 seconds. But, in our case we would hit BMC_READY within ~10 seconds. And then we would apply the restore policy. 

Hence, this patch ensures that we wait for the time defined by the user.
Done
